description:
FILED s449r (Opus round-7 agent R) from the #532 probe battery.  PRE-EXISTING:
identical on a c8a8311 worktree, so #532 neither caused nor fixed it.

    sub G {99}  open(G, ">", "/dev/stdout") or die;  print G "to-g\n";
        perl  99            (perl CALLS G and prints its value)
        PCL   to-g          (PCL writes through the handle)

    sub G {99}  open(G, "<", "/etc/hostname") or die;  my $l = <G>;
        perl  undef         (r=0)
        PCL   a line        (r=1)

WHY IT MATTERS: #532 established the asymmetry PCL now implements for the two
`*`-prototype slots -- a BUILTIN handle slot lets the HANDLE win even against
a declared sub (`sub FILE1 () {42}; tell FILE1` is -1), a USER `(*)` sub CALLS
the declared name.  These two probes say perl's print/readline slots side with
the USER half, not the builtin half, and PCL sides with the builtin half in
both.  So the rule is three-valued, not two, and the third value is not
written down anywhere.

WHERE: the `$is_fh_func` skip near the head of `Pl::PExpr::handle_subcalls`
(the block that returns for a word preceded by print/say/printf or a `(*)`
prototype) never asks `_bareword_callable_here`, and `gen_readline_form`'s
bareword branch does not either.  #532's fix deliberately did NOT touch them:
that skip returns BEFORE the registry exit it narrowed, and widening it is a
separate, print-shaped question with its own inverses (a name that is a
CONSTANT, an imported sub, a not-yet-declared sub).

BAR: the two probes above plus the inverses (no sub declared; a sub declared
BELOW the print, which perl compiling top-down does not see; `print STDOUT`
with a `sub STDOUT` declared), corpus-diff + the 1036-file A/B with every DIFF
explained, and rows beside the #532 block in Pl/t/user-unary-01.t.  Family:
#266 / #495 (what a bare WORD means in operand position).
